title: Exact binomial hypothesis test
intro: Use the null probability and include the observed count in the correct tail.

beats.spoken: Eight of sixteen independent checks pass. Does the pass rate exceed the usual twenty-five percent?
beats.coach: Eight successes in 16 independent trials. H₀: p = 0.25. Hₐ: p > 0.25.

beats.spoken: Higher is the alternative, so look at eight or more. Include the observed eight.
beats.coach: Under H₀, X ~ Bin(16, 0.25). Count the observed eight and every count above it: P(X ≥ 8).

beats.spoken: On a Calculator page choose Probability, Distributions, then Binomial C D F.
beats.coach: On a Calculator page: Menu → 5 Probability → 5 Distributions → E Binomial Cdf.

beats.spoken: Enter sixteen trials and the null probability, zero point two five, not the sample proportion of eight out of sixteen.
beats.coach: Enter 16 trials and the null probability 0.25, not the observed proportion 8/16.

beats.spoken: Set the lower bound to eight and the upper bound to sixteen. Both are included.
beats.coach: Lower bound 8, upper bound 16. Binomial Cdf includes both endpoints.

beats.spoken: Enter inserts the command. Enter again finds the whole upper tail.
beats.coach: First Enter inserts binomCdf(16,0.25,8,16). The second Enter evaluates the command.

beats.spoken: The tail probability is about zero point zero two seven one. It is below zero point zero five: reject the null hypothesis.
beats.coach: The complete upper-tail probability is about 0.0271. Since it is below 0.05, reject H₀.

beats.spoken: For a lower alternative, count from zero through the observation. The LCD still shows the upper-tail example.
beats.coach: For a lower-sided alternative, count from 0 through the observation. The LCD deliberately stays on this original upper-tail example.
